title: Connectivity is progressing globally, but affordability, usage, and network quality continue to divide digital participation
source_unit: International Telecommunication Union, Measuring Digital Development: The ICT Development Index 2026
geography: 159 economies compared on universal and meaningful connectivity, affordability, Internet use, and quality of connectivity

denominator.unit: economies covered by the ICT Development Index 2026

global_progress.value: the global average ICT Development Index score increased again

strongest_improvement.value: the strongest improvements were recorded in low- and lower-middle-income economies

meaningful_connectivity.value: the index tracks progress toward universal and meaningful connectivity rather than access alone

observations.method: ITU composite-index comparison of connectivity and digital-development indicators across 159 economies.
observations.uncertainty: An index average can improve while individual countries, groups, or dimensions stagnate; it does not measure every user's quality of experience, safety, or ability to convert access into welfare.
observations.subgroup: Low- and lower-middle-income economies, rural and remote communities, households facing affordability barriers, workers, students, and public-service users.
observations.counterinterpretation: Average progress can reflect genuine diffusion of infrastructure and skills, while remaining compatible with persistent local exclusion and unequal service quality.

denominator.unit: economy-level affordability, Internet-use, and connectivity-access indicators

internet_use_gap.value: significant disparities persist in Internet use

conversion_problem.value: nominal coverage does not automatically become meaningful participation when prices, devices, skills, or service conditions restrict use

observations.method: ITU analysis of digital-development dimensions including access, affordability, usage, and quality.
observations.uncertainty: Economy-level disparities do not identify household budgets, individual use motives, or causal effects of price changes on education, work, health, or political participation.
observations.subgroup: Low-income households, women and girls, rural residents, persons with disabilities, students, migrants, and small firms.
observations.counterinterpretation: Affordability constraints can be offset by public access, shared devices, community networks, competition, subsidies, or falling prices, though those routes may vary in reliability and privacy.

observations.period: 2026; quality of connectivity and digital agency

denominator.unit: economy-level network quality, service reliability, and meaningful-connectivity frame

quality_gap.value: significant disparities persist in the quality of connectivity

quality_to_agency.value: network quality shapes whether connectivity supports education, work, public services, communication, and cultural participation

infrastructure_dependence.value: digital participation depends on networks, devices, electricity, affordability, skills, and institutional service design

observations.method: ITU composite measurement and comparative interpretation of connectivity quality and meaningful-use conditions.
observations.uncertainty: The index does not establish causal effects of network quality on individual outcomes or separate all dimensions of reliability, latency, privacy, safety, and resilience.
observations.subgroup: Remote communities, public institutions, digital workers, students, businesses, people dependent on online services, and areas exposed to outages or disaster.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower-quality connections can still provide high-value access for some uses, and local innovation or offline complements can reduce dependence on premium networks.

denominator.unit: digital connectivity, platform participation, public services, work, and cultural-life frame

participation_surface.value: meaningful connectivity expands the surface through which people work, learn, consume, organize, access services, and maintain social ties

risk_surface.value: expanded connectivity also increases exposure to platform dependence, data extraction, misinformation, exclusion, and attention competition

policy_question.value: the open policy question is whether digital development produces agency and public capacity rather than access without control

observations.method: Program-level synthesis connecting ITU connectivity dimensions to platform, work, consumer, cultural, and public-service themes.
observations.uncertainty: This is an analytical bridge, not a causal estimate from the ITU index; it does not claim that connectivity automatically improves welfare, trust, or political voice.
observations.subgroup: Internet users and non-users, households, workers, firms, platform operators, governments, schools, health systems, and cultural organizations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Connectivity can enable mutual aid, public accountability, local enterprise, cultural exchange, and service access when governance and user control are strong.

related_sources.claim: ITU Facts and Figures provides complementary global indicators on Internet use, access, and digital divides.
ITU ICT indicators provide the underlying comparative statistical context for digital-development measurement.

boundary: This record adds a global digital-infrastructure, affordability, quality, platform-participation, and institutional-capacity route. It uses an economy-level composite index and report synthesis, not respondent-level Internet diaries, individual transaction data, causal welfare estimates, or proof that connectivity automatically creates agency.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official ITU ICT Development Index 2026 materials were reviewed for 159-economy coverage, global-average progress, low- and lower-middle-income improvement, and persistent affordability, Internet-use, and connectivity-quality disparities.
